clue.text: Cheers A bit embarrassing for abstainers

indicators.note: embarrassing here means thrown into confusion, so the letters of these words get muddled up

explanation.surface: A toast of 'Cheers!' makes a group of teetotallers rather uncomfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embarrassing' rearranges CHEERS A BIT. The Rechabites are a temperance friendly society whose members pledge to avoid alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rechabites, named after a biblical family who refused wine, are a temperance order, so its members shun alcohol.

clue.text: One on another side

parts.note: a player in a cricket or football team is one on a side; the whole team is the number that side contains

explanation.surface: A single person standing on the opposing team.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket and football teams have this many players, so the team is itself called by the number.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football team is called by its number of players.

clue.text: Lower city type?

parts.note: lower is not 'less high' but 'one that lows, moos', so a breed of cattle that is also the name of a city

explanation.surface: A downmarket sort of urban person.
explanation.walkthrough: A cow lows, so a 'lower' is a cow. Hereford is a cathedral city in the west of England and its name is also a beef breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-and-white beef cattle breed takes its name from an English cathedral city.

clue.text: It might carry instruction in some form

definitions.text: It might carry instruction in some form

parts.words: It might carry instruction in some form
parts.note: form means a school class, so this is what holds the teacher's chalked lessons in a classroom

explanation.surface: Something that conveys teaching in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class year.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark board in classrooms is chalked with lessons for the pupils of a form.

clue.text: Main transport well loaded?

parts.note: main is the sea, and the ships carry oil from a well; tanked up also means drunk

explanation.surface: A remark about crowded public transport, or a drunkard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is a literary word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships built to carry oil or other liquid in bulk across the sea.

clue.text: Pole used on river as support

parts.note: S is south, one of the poles
the Tay is a river in Scotland

explanation.surface: A punt pole used on the water as a prop.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a brace or rope that holds something up, a support.

clue.text: Killers face terrible charges ?

parts.note: reads like murderers facing criminal charges, but these killers face charging bulls in the ring

explanation.surface: Murderers are brought to trial on serious counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullfighters who kill the bull stand against its frightening rushes.

clue.text: Player or conductor ?

definitions.meaning: the principal male actor in a production
someone guiding a man, as a lead or a guide does

explanation.surface: A performer or a bandleader.
explanation.definitionFit: The star male actor is the top player, and one who guides a person conducts him.

clue.text: One in business makes a vehement speech

indicators.note: the word in tells us the single digit sits inside the commercial word

parts.note: trade is commerce, business
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone in commerce delivers an angry harangue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long, angry outburst of words, a vehement speech.

clue.text: Apple, the fruit one gets in the island

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

indicators.note: gets in tells us the numeral enters the name of the island

parts.note: the Isle of Man, often just Man in crosswords
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: An apple named for a pear-like fruit grown on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a British Crown dependency in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearmain is an old variety of apple, as in Worcester Pearmain.

clue.text: Something depressing which may result in strain ?

definitions.text: Something depressing which may result in strain ?

parts.words: Something depressing which may result in strain ?
parts.note: reads like a cause of stress, but it means a set of keys pressed down on a piano which produces a musical strain, a tune

explanation.surface: Something gloomy that might cause nervous tension.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano's set of keys is pressed down, and playing it yields a strain, meaning a melody.

clue.text: Remarkable Scottish characters from Runcorn

indicators.note: characters from means some consecutive letters are taken out of the town name that follows

explanation.surface: Notable Scots folk come from the Cheshire town of Runcorn.
explanation.walkthrough: Runcorn is an industrial town in Cheshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Unco is a Scots word meaning remarkable or extraordinary.

clue.text: Such philosophical works as Dupin has translated

indicators.note: translated here means the letters of these words are turned into a new form

explanation.surface: Poe's detective Dupin has rendered such philosophical texts into another language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges AS DUPIN HAS. Dupin is Edgar Allan Poe's detective.
explanation.definitionFit: The Upanishads are ancient Sanskrit texts of Hindu philosophy.

clue.text: Old 'measure used by John for whisky

definitions.meaning: a former unit of length equal to a third of an inch
John ... is the traditional personification of malt liquor and whisky

explanation.surface: An antique unit is what a man called John uses for his whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: John Barleycorn is the folk-song figure who stands for the barley crop and the drink made from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A grain of barley was once a standard unit of length, and the grain is also the spirit's source, hence the folk name for whisky.

clue.text: Interpretation of former state of affairs

parts.note: ex means former
a position is a situation, a state of affairs

explanation.surface: An explanation of how things used to stand.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposition is an explanation or account setting out meaning.

clue.text: Articles written about Muslim magistrate from Nova Scotia

indicators.note: written about tells us the two short words are placed around the judge

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
an is the other form of the indefinite article
a cadi (qadi) is a judge in Islamic law

explanation.surface: Newspaper pieces covering an Islamic judge who hails from eastern Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' looks like newspaper pieces but means the grammatical articles; 'written about' places them around the Islamic judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Acadia was the old French colony covering Nova Scotia, so its people are Acadians.

clue.text: Poor Nesta carries complaint from the islands

indicators.note: carries means the reworked name holds the ailment inside it
poor signals the name's letters are in bad shape, rearranged

parts.note: an ill is an ailment, a complaint

explanation.surface: Unfortunate Nesta brings back an illness from her Caribbean trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges the name to ANTES, and 'carries' holds the ailment inside it. The Antilles are the Caribbean island chain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antilles are the chain of islands in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Marsupial presents a very big problem after work

indicators.note: after tells us the problem pieces come behind the abbreviation for work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
OS stands for outsize, very big
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: An animal that brings up a huge difficulty once the labour is done.
explanation.definitionFit: The opossum of the Americas carries its young in a pouch, as kangaroos do.

clue.text: Writer George meets composer in Cheshire

parts.note: George Sand was the pen name of a French novelist
J. S. Bach was a German composer

explanation.surface: A novelist encounters a composer in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheshire is a county in north-west England; the definition is a place in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandbach is a market town found within Cheshire, England.

clue.text: Enliven a rising, batting team, possibly

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a batsman batting in cricket is in

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of the next word may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Liven up a cricket team on the rise as it bats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns IN to NI, and 'possibly' rearranges TEAM to MATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate is to bring life to, to enliven.

clue.text: French officials appear mean to workers

parts.note: to mean to do something is to intend it
worker ants, so workers are ants in crosswords

explanation.surface: Officials across the Channel seem stingy towards their staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like stingy, but 'mean to' is to intend.
explanation.definitionFit: Intendants were royal administrators sent to govern the provinces of old France.

clue.text: Time for watch is after 2, perhaps

definitions.text: Time for watch is after 2, perhaps

parts.words: Time for watch is after 2, perhaps
parts.note: the ship's ... watch is literally after this hour, and twelve is the time it follows; 2 o'clock, say, is after it

explanation.surface: A remark about when the next watch begins, at some point after two.
explanation.walkthrough: At sea the afternoon watch runs from midday to four.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is twelve o'clock, the hour that two in the afternoon comes after.

clue.text: Blue, so resorted to a dagger

indicators.note: resorted read as re-sorted, sorted again, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Feeling low, someone turned to a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resorted' is not 'turned to' but 're-sorted', so it rearranges BLUE SO.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelus is the dagger sign used in printing to mark a note or a doubtful passage.

clue.text: Clue for a jolly holiday?

parts.note: a cheerful school break, read as a hint: jolly is a half of a phrase or term like jolly good

explanation.surface: Someone asking for a hint about where to take a fun break.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools the break in the middle of each term is a short holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A short school holiday falls in the middle of each British school term.

clue.text: Understand about a pound rise in fish

indicators.note: in a down clue rise means the whole result is read upwards
about tells us the verb goes round the abbreviation for a pound

parts.note: to see is to understand
L, from Latin libra, is a pound

explanation.surface: Grasping how a pound increase affects the fish trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside SEE to give SLEE, and 'rise' turns that upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long, snake-like fish.

clue.text: Kind friend translated message

parts.note: friend put into French gives ami
a cable is a telegram, a message

explanation.surface: A kindly companion decodes a note.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable means friendly and well-disposed, so kind.

clue.text: Engine one found in Leeds perhaps

indicators.note: found in tells us the numeral sits inside the reworked letters of the city name
perhaps signals the city's letters may be arranged differently

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A motor discovered in a Yorkshire city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges LEEDS to DESEL, and 'found in' puts I inside it. Leeds is a city in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A diesel is a compression-ignition engine, or a locomotive driven by one.

clue.text: Main pursuit appears, austere — has entered church

parts.note: stern means severe, austere

indicators.note: entered means the word has goes inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chase appears, as a severe figure walks into church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea, so a main pursuit is a naval one.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval chase where one ship follows directly behind another, astern, is a pursuit at sea.
